verdict.rationale: ROS 2 is API- and CLI-first. Its client libraries expose its core functionality, and the CLI covers nodes, topics, services, parameters and bags. The bare-bones install ships communication libraries and command-line tools with no GUI tools, which implies the core works headlessly. However, no documentation states parity between the GUI tools (RViz, shown in the desktop install) and the API, and several features are limited to C++. Missing for 10: an explicit statement or evidence that everything in the GUI tools (RViz/visualization) is reachable programmatically; independent hands-on corroboration of parity; non-C++ coverage for lifecycle, composition and content filtering.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: client libraries expose to users the core functionality that makes ROS "ROS"
The main entry point for the tools is the command ros2, which itself has various sub-commands for introspecting and working with nodes, topics, services, and more.
ROS-Base Install (Bare Bones): Communication libraries, message packages, command line tools. No GUI tools.
It also provides a Python API for reading from and writing to a bag from your own source code.
